verdicts.evidence: The callout [data-testid=brief-insight] renders with its accent - background rgb(234,244,251), 3px left border rgb(61,152,211) - but it does not argue. It is headed 'Nobody has argued with this yet' and says the Studio cannot tell you whether the request names a solution because nothing here has read it, then offers 'Ask it to argue with this'. That path is real and now honest about why it cannot complete: [data-testid=brief-assistant-signed-out] renders beneath it saying '<ext>'s pod has no credential, so anything this screen sends it comes back "Not logged in - Please run /login" and no ## The challenge is ever written. Open the workspace terminal, run /login, and ask again.' That message is the third of three states - the code distinguishes not-asked (login null), could-not-ask (read:false) and read-and-empty, and only the last asserts anything - and it is the state that renders here, correctly, because the pod's claude really is logged out.
verdicts.defect: Nothing in the Studio weighs the request against the problem statement, so the callout asks for the argument rather than making it. It can carry one that the assistant writes into '## The challenge', but no pod in this environment has a credential, so on every real brief here it says nobody has argued rather than the design's 'this ticket asked for a solution, and here is why building it as written misses the point'.

[data-testid=verify-progress] read 0/4, went to 1/4 on a Yes and 2/4 on a No, and stayed at 2/4 when I answered a third criterion 'Can't tell' - which is the rule the feature states. It fell back to 3/4 when I moved one of the four off an answered verdict.

The pane is a real iframe, not an image: src is the extension's own dev server through the apiserver proxy (.../barn-base-extension:8005/proxy/), 485x555 in the panel, and fetching that URL from the page returned 200 with 2847 bytes of the dashboard's index HTML. Its footer also reports what it is showing against the change ('pages/Home.vue differs from the baseline. Point the preview at a page one of them renders and it is outlined here.').

Now implemented, and it moves the line rather than deleting it. With a brief whose non-goals were '- No zebrastripe rendering of any table' and '- No alerting of any kind', and a change adding a line containing 'zebrastripe' to pages/Home.vue, the card warned on that term and offered 'That is fine - add it to the brief' [data-testid=verify-accept-drift-zebrastripe]. Pressing it rewrote BRIEF.md, and the whole diff of the file is two hunks: the line left '## What we are deliberately not doing' and arrived under '## What changes for them' as '- No zebrastripe rendering of any table (accepted during verification on 2026-08-23 by admin)'. Nothing else moved - the criteria section, the '## Verification' block with its recorded verdicts, a hand-written '## Hand written by w4bf' section and '## Who asked' were all byte-identical afterwards. The warning cleared on the spot: the card re-read as the clear state for the remaining term. And unsaved work on the page survived - I had left one criterion on an unsaved "Can't tell" and typed an unsaved note into another before pressing it, and after the write the progress chip, all four verdicts and the note text were exactly as I had left them.

The amber-bordered warning renders with the heading 'Scope', a '2 files changed' chip, and the paragraph 'This change adds lines that mention what the brief said it was deliberately not doing. A word match is not proof of anything - it is a place to look.' It is genuinely automatic and genuinely computed: it found the term I had planted in an added line of pages/Home.vue and named the file, and when no added line matched it switched to the success state naming the terms it had looked for. It also has an 'unstated' state for a brief with no non-goals and a 'nothing-changed' state for a tree with no added lines.

Now implemented, and it explicitly does not touch the brief. Pressed 'Remove it' [data-testid=verify-remove-drift-alerting]: the toast read 'Asked the assistant to take "alerting" back out. It replies in the workspace terminal, and this card will still warn until the lines are gone.' Capturing the tmux pane in the extension's pod shows the prompt arrived in full, including the coincidence caveat ('If the match is a coincidence and nothing there does it, change nothing and say so - a word match is not proof. Do not edit BRIEF.md: the brief is the reviewer's to change.'). BRIEF.md before and after the press was byte-identical, and the warning stayed up. The assistant answers 'Not logged in - Please run /login', which is the known credential-less pod, not a defect in this control.

With criterion 2 answered No and a note typed, pressed 'Send this back to the assistant'. The toast read 'Sent to the assistant working on this extension. It replies in the workspace terminal.' and the pod's tmux pane holds the whole thing: the criterion text, 'It was checked at /home', the reviewer's note quoted verbatim, and 'Do not edit BRIEF.md - the verdicts are recorded by the reviewer.' The card gains no persistent 'sent' marker afterwards - only the transient loading state and the toast - so the 'marked as sent' half of the design is not drawn.

Now implemented, and it is honest about a failed write. Success path: pressing 'Send the whole list back' recorded the pass into BRIEF.md first (the '## Verification' block held all four verdicts with their routes and the failed one's note) and then put the same list to the pod's assistant - the tmux pane shows '(1) [Met] ... [checked at /home]; (2) [Not met] ... - the reviewer wrote: "..."; (3) ...; (4) ...' - with the toast 'All 4 verdicts are in BRIEF.md and the list has gone to the assistant... nothing has left the review queue.' Failed-write path: I made BRIEF.md unwritable to the uid the pod execs as (root-owned, mode 444) and pressed it again. It showed the error toast 'Could not record the verification', made no success claim, and sent nothing - the pod's pane gained no new prompt. That is save() returning false and gating the hand-off.

Pressed 'Show me' on criterion 3: the pinned preview's path field became /home and the pane header read 'Criterion 3'. Pressing it on criterion 1 moved the header to 'Criterion 1'. The preview iframe is the running extension, so it is driving the real thing rather than a mock.

With one criterion answered No the button was disabled with title '1 criterion is answered No. A No holds the sign-off open until it is answered Yes.', and with unanswered criteria it said '<n> criteria have not been looked at yet.' With all four Yes it enabled; pressing it closed the gate for real - the footer row became check-marked 'Outcome sign-off - Default Admin - just now', the line read 'Signed off on 2026-08-23 by Default Admin. Changing a verdict takes the sign-off back.', and the barn-review-<ext> ConfigMap gained signoffs.outcome with verdict approved, principal local://user-btc48, name Default Admin, the timestamp and the commit sha - which is the record the distribution gate reads.

Both rows render with their own state, and both are read from the review record rather than drawn. Before either gate: 'Code review - not signed off' (empty dot) and 'Outcome sign-off - you - in progress' (empty dot). After approving the code on screen 12: the code row became check-marked 'Code review - Default Admin - just now'. After signing off: the outcome row became check-marked too. And the code row went stale correctly - after the sign-off was given against an older commit the outcome row read 'Default Admin approved an earlier commit, so it no longer covers this one'.

Clicked each of the three segments on a criterion. Exactly one stays selected (aria-pressed true on one, false on the other two) and the colours match: Yes fills rgb(62,140,79) green, No fills red, Can't tell stays neutral. The progress chip and the footer sentence moved with every change.

Checked all three of the stated consequences. The counter does not increment - it was 2/4 before and 2/4 after answering a third criterion 'Can't tell', and the footer switched from '1 not met' to '1 could not be judged'. It does not block: with the only No changed to Can't tell the blocked note disappeared and 'Sign off on the outcome' became enabled, footer reading 'Nothing is holding the sign-off open.' The badge does keep the plain criterion number rather than a tick or a cross. The one deviation is the colour: the badge is verify__badge--unsure, amber rgb(201,162,39), where the design calls for grey.
